acp.reviewRecommendation: Accept restricted account for local Alpha; Base Sepolia Beta remains blocked

findings.title: Owner-signed EntryPoint calls can execute arbitrary account targets
findings.description: N.1 found that the account blocked direct owner execution but allowed any valid owner-signed EntryPoint UserOperation to call execute(address,uint256,bytes) with an arbitrary target. N.2 remediates this by binding each account to an immutable approved ActionGate and rejecting non-ActionGate targets and non-verifyAndConsume selectors.
findings.attackScenario: A stolen or misused owner key signs a UserOperation that bypasses Runtime policy and calls a non-ActionGate target.
findings.impact: Account funds or approvals can be used outside PhilCore Runtime authorization.
findings.likelihood: medium before production custody; high if owner key is exposed
findings.evidence: contracts/base/erc4337/PhilCore4337Account.sol enforces approvedActionGate and verifyAndConsume selector. test/unit/philcore-erc4337-security-review-n1.test.cjs proves arbitrary owner-signed EntryPoint targets, wrong selectors, and account-self nesting do not execute.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Keep ActionGate-restricted account model for Beta and preserve Runtime validation as defense in depth.

findings.title: Production custody, rotation, and recovery for Beta ECDSA owner are missing
findings.description: N.3 adds local Alpha Device Vault encrypted ECDSA custody and one-time exact-hash M.10 signing sessions. N.4 adds restricted local Alpha on-chain owner rotation and delayed recovery. N.5 adds local Alpha recovery-authority custody, approval, recovery-only signing, and local EntryPoint recovery workflow evidence. N.8 adds bounded delayed recovery-authority rotation. Beta recovery-authority custody approval, external audit, deployment controls, threshold/modular production recovery, and stronger stolen-key response remain incomplete.
findings.attackScenario: A lost key strands the account or a stolen key controls it.
findings.reproduction: npm run test:device-vault-ecdsa-signing && npm run test:erc4337-recovery && npm run test:recovery-authority-custody
findings.recommendedRemediation: Approve a Beta recovery-authority custody model, externally review N.8 recovery-authority rotation, implement/adopt threshold or modular recovery for production, and restrict Beta to disposable no-meaningful-asset accounts until audit and deployment gates pass.

findings.title: Custom account and factory are unaudited
findings.description: The account/factory are custom local/Beta contracts and have not received external review.
findings.attackScenario: A subtle account abstraction bug is exploited after public deployment.
findings.impact: Potential account compromise or execution failure.
findings.evidence: Manual review only; no external audit.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Prepare external audit package after N.2 remediation.

findings.title: M.11 receipt monitoring allowed permissive default execution evidence
findings.description: Receipt monitoring could produce a successful bounded receipt without explicit inner execution, nullifier, and consumer verifiers.
findings.attackScenario: A caller treats successful inclusion as sufficient proof of PhilCore execution.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Require explicit verifiers for successful receipt monitoring.

findings.title: Dependency audit reports unresolved advisories
findings.description: N.1 npm audit reported 22 advisories. N.2 patched direct ethers and OpenZeppelin dependencies, reducing the count to 20. N.6 applied a non-forced lockfile remediation that reduced the count to 16 and removed the original lodash and Hardhat-nested ws high advisory groups. N.7 formally classifies serialize-javascript, tmp, and undici as development-tooling-only exposure and accepts the risk temporarily with controls pending a reviewed Hardhat/toolchain migration.
findings.attackScenario: Vulnerable tooling or libraries are exploited in development, CI, or deployment flows.
findings.impact: Development environment compromise or library risk depending on package exposure.
findings.evidence: config/security/philcore-npm-audit-report.json and config/security/philcore-dependency-exposure.json after N.7 report 16 advisories: 10 low, 3 moderate, 3 high, 0 critical. No remaining high advisory is classified as production runtime exposure.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Keep dev tooling excluded from production runtime packaging, run only on trusted inputs, and perform Architecture Change Control before any Hardhat 3/toolchain migration.

findings.title: Pinned Slither environment required before Beta
findings.description: Slither was not installed in N.1. N.6 adds and verifies a repository-local Python virtual environment for Slither 0.10.4, plus machine-readable Slither and custom invariant reports.
findings.reproduction: npm run security:setup-slither && npm run security:slither && npm run security:philcore-contract-invariants
findings.recommendedRemediation: Keep Slither setup reproducible in CI and preserve triage evidence before Beta.

findings.title: Authorized consumer contracts are trusted execution modules
findings.description: ActionGate verifies authorization and calls the authorized consumer, but consumer semantics are outside ActionGate.
findings.attackScenario: Runtime authorizes an unreviewed malicious consumer.
findings.likelihood: low with reviewed consumers; higher without a consumer catalog
findings.evidence: PhilAdversarialAuthorizationConsumer tests demonstrate consumer-controlled behavior while preserving ActionGate atomicity.
findings.recommendedRemediation: Maintain reviewed consumer catalog and bind Runtime capabilities to consumer identities.

findings.title: PhilMintPassConsumer can lock forwarded ETH
findings.description: Slither reports `locked-ether` for PhilMintPassConsumer because `consumePhilAuthorization(...)` is payable through the authorization consumer interface. N.7 remediates the actual retained-value risk by rejecting nonzero `msg.value` before mint state changes.
findings.attackScenario: If a future authorized mint path forwards ETH to PhilMintPassConsumer, the call now reverts atomically instead of minting and retaining value.
findings.impact: Value-bearing mint paths are prohibited. The shared payable interface may continue to trigger a static-analysis heuristic, but the implementation is zero-value-only.
findings.likelihood: low after N.7 zero-value guard and tests
findings.recommendedRemediation: Keep PhilMintPassConsumer zero-value-only. Any value-bearing mint/pass purchase flow requires Architecture Change Control and a reviewed forwarding/refund model.
